h: Turning Brodie into a full Moray day
p: Brodie sits just off the A96 between Forres and Nairn, which makes it dead easy to drop into a road trip along the Moray coast. Give yourself at least half a day if you want the tour, the Playful Garden and a proper wander round the grounds. Rush it and you'll miss the best bits, especially if the kids get stuck into the garden, which they will.

Beyond the castle walls there are woodland paths and a pond to stroll round, so it's well worth packing decent shoes. Daffodil season in spring is the showpiece, but the estate works through the year, with autumn colour in the trees and a good bit of fresh air whatever the month. Bring a layer, because that wind off the Moray Firth can have a nip to it even on bright days.

Once you're done, Forres is only a few minutes away and has plenty to fill an afternoon. Sueno's Stone, a towering carved Pictish stone now protected under glass, is a real head-turner and costs nothing to look at. Grant Park is beautifully kept with its flower displays, and you can climb Cluny Hill to Nelson's Tower for views over the town and out to the firth.

Fancy a bit of coast? Findhorn is a short drive north, with its sweeping bay, sandy beach and big skies, and Nairn's beaches are just along the road in the other direction. Put Brodie in the morning, a beach walk in the afternoon and fish and chips to finish, and that's a cracking Moray day sorted.
